title: Separate market-data admission from market-data discovery

options.label: Official-only production lane
options.upside: Keeps the operational evidence set tightly controlled and avoids unreviewed third-party terms.
options.downside: The official historical record may not contain the market fields or open/close history needed for price-residual gates.

options.label: Licensed odds archive/feed
options.upside: Could provide quote timestamps, event identifiers, terms clarity and open/close history in one approved source.
options.downside: Procurement cost and the feed's exact market/jurisdiction coverage still need checking.

options.label: Isolated third-party research lane
options.upside: The repository already contains historical line fields that may support exploratory comparisons if terms and lineage permit.
options.downside: The existing game log is not official NFL data, has no separate open/close pair, and does not establish a legal/redistribution right.

recommendation: Do not change the current production gate. Prepare a source/terms decision; if third-party data is later approved, keep it quarantined and labeled research-only until separate validation and rights checks pass.
what_supports_recommendation: Both a third-party historical file and a live first-party operator page were found, but neither establishes an approved, timestamped open/close series for this project.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_admission: Written terms allow the intended storage/transformation/use; quote time, line convention, event mapping and jurisdiction are explicit; hashes and row counts reconcile.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_continued_block: Terms are unavailable or restrictive, quote timestamps/location are missing, opening and closing are conflated, or independent row checks fail.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — no market policy, data source or model input changed.

title: Represent injury coverage per club and per status type

options.label: League endpoint only
options.upside: Simple and consistent source path.
options.downside: The requested Week 11 endpoint currently returns Week 10, so it cannot establish league-wide current coverage.

options.label: League endpoint plus explicit club fallback
options.upside: Can preserve useful club-level evidence such as the Texans/Colts Week 11 practice report.
options.downside: Requires 32-club coverage accounting and strict separation of practice, game-status and inactive fields.

options.label: Wait for a complete league report
options.upside: Avoids stitching partial pages into a misleading complete report.
options.downside: Leaves decision readiness blocked while some official club pages publish sooner.

recommendation: Use explicit per-club states and a dated club fallback only as a partial source; keep unknown clubs blank and do not publish an all-clear until the coverage gate is met.
what_supports_recommendation: The official league route served Week 10 while an official club page had Week 11 practice tables for two clubs; the fields are not interchangeable.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_fallback: A complete official club-by-club read can preserve each source date, practice/game/inactive status type and explicit not-published state.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_waiting: If club pages cannot be captured reliably or coverage cannot be audited, keep the feature blocked rather than blending incomplete reads.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — no existing availability data or capture workflow changed.

title: Make capture intervals derived facts, not hand-written durations

options.label: Correct the prose manually
options.upside: Fast if one known typo is confirmed.
options.downside: Does not prevent future timestamp/duration drift across pages and coordination notes.

options.label: Compute interval from two timestamped captures
options.upside: One reproducible result can drive tables and prose; tests can reject conflicting text.
options.downside: Requires establishing which saved captures/timestamps are canonical first.

recommendation: Reconcile the source pair first, then generate the duration from machine-readable UTC timestamps and test the result; do not guess which of 49 hours or 1 hour 13 minutes was intended.
what_supports_recommendation: The stored pair spans 25 hours 13 minutes, while the prior pages and coordination prose state two other intervals.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_automatic_calculation: The original immutable captures confirm both stored timestamps and a deterministic calculation yields 25 hours 13 minutes.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_different_duration: A raw source log proves one timestamp belongs to another read or was mistyped; then replace the pair and recompute, not just the prose.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — the prior desk timestamps and copy were not edited.

title: Require complete transaction coverage before absence-based roster claims

options.label: Use monthly result-page captures as-is
options.upside: Low effort and preserves what the page visibly returned.
options.downside: A 25-row cap can create false negatives; an absent row is not evidence no move occurred.

options.label: Paginate or query per club with a declared date window
options.upside: Supports defensible positive and negative searches with row counts and boundaries.
options.downside: Requires more reads and careful deduplication/source logging.

recommendation: Use the paginated/per-club route for future absence claims; label the existing Baltimore IR claim unresolved and leave player position blank unless separately sourced.
what_supports_recommendation: The prior reserve capture contains only 25 rows per month, has a date gap, and does not publish player position in its stored schema.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_a_negative_conclusion: All pages for the declared window are accounted for, the official results provide a complete matching search, and every claimed position is separately sourced.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_remaining_unresolved: Any pagination gap, source truncation or ambiguous player-position mapping remains.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — no roster register or existing claim was rewritten.

title: Treat the Chargers–Ravens final as a delta, then re-run full feed reconciliation

options.label: Apply the one-game delta only
options.upside: Corrects the one known pending fixture quickly.
options.downside: Does not prove the rest of the historical feed is complete or club-code joins are sound.

options.label: Rebuild the declared cutoff feed and reconcile 32 clubs
options.upside: Tests the full data set after the new final and can expose duplicates, dropped games and alias defects.
options.downside: More work than a one-row patch and must preserve the exact cutoff/source set.

recommendation: Keep the current one-row delta as evidence, but do not call the season record current until the entire feed is rebuilt and reconciled club by club against same-cut official standings.
what_supports_recommendation: Two official NFL pages now show Chargers 23, Ravens 20 Final; the earlier desk snapshot predated that final, and this dossier does not rebuild the complete feed.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_current_record_claim: A deterministic full-feed rebuild contains each final exactly once and every club record matches official standings at the same cutoff.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_remaining_partial: Any unresolved game alias, duplicate/missing fixture or standings mismatch keeps the full-feed status blocked.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — this dossier records a delta but does not mutate the prior result feed.

title: Keep Game Book rows out of the data pipeline until rights are explicit

options.label: Request written permission
options.upside: Could preserve a high-value official game-level source if the intended uses are authorized.
options.downside: Permission may be unavailable, narrow or costly to administer.

options.label: Use a separately licensed/authorized feed
options.upside: May provide a clear data-use scope for structured fields.
options.downside: Requires finding and verifying a suitable source and its coverage.

options.label: Do not use Game Book player-level rows
options.upside: Avoids unauthorized copying/modeling while preserving official score/Game Center use where allowed.
options.downside: Starter/participation features remain blocked without another source.

recommendation: Do not copy or model from the PDF unless written permission specifically covers the intended fields, retention, training and display; otherwise choose an expressly authorized alternative or keep those features blank.
what_supports_recommendation: The PDF itself says other use beyond assisting media coverage is prohibited without written permission.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_use: Written permission or a license explicitly covers every planned use and field.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_exclusion: Permission is absent, ambiguous, or excludes persistent storage, derivative modeling or public display.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — no Game Book player-level data is copied or used by this review.

title: Add a semantic consistency gate for model metadata and readiness statuses

options.label: Manual review before each publication
options.upside: Fast to start and can catch obvious prose/table drift.
options.downside: A manual pass can miss stale copies across the card, forecasts and summary.

options.label: Derive narrative values/status from canonical data and test invariants
options.upside: Prevents mismatched model coefficients and a MET requirement with an undefined residual from silently shipping.
options.downside: Requires identifying the true canonical source and expressing status logic explicitly.

recommendation: Resolve the -0.52/-0.46 model coefficient from a frozen refit, and keep REQ-04 blocked until approved market values populate the residual. Generate or test all dependent summaries against those canonical outputs.
what_supports_recommendation: The prior model card/forecasts disagree with Q-05/executive prose, and REQ-04 is marked MET while its own evidence says undefined and market columns are blank.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_close: A deterministic refit establishes one coefficient and every dependent output matches; an admitted price then yields a numeric residual.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_block: Any remaining mismatch, blank market quote or undefined residual keeps the readiness status partial/blocked.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — model coefficients, statuses and prior artifacts were not changed.

title: Keep strategy standings shadow-only until uncertainty-aware gates pass

options.label: Rank by win rate or ROI now
options.upside: Easy to explain and immediately populated.
options.downside: Zero settled observations for the reviewed registrations cannot support a performance claim; small-sample variance and staking can dominate.

options.label: Use proper scores, uncertainty and chronological holdouts
options.upside: Measures probability quality against baselines and exposes uncertainty and leakage risk.
options.downside: Requires more prospective/chronological data and disciplined pre-registration.

recommendation: Keep the current entries in shadow; do not put backtest results on the leaderboard. Before promotion, freeze rule hashes and use proper probability scores, baselines, uncertainty bounds, calibration and demotion gates; report staking separately.
what_supports_recommendation: P-01/P-02/P-03 each have 13 forecasts and zero settlements, with blank score fields; the model card calls the model a shadow baseline.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_promotion: A pre-registered strategy clears the required chronological sample, proper-score benchmark, calibration/uncertainty bounds, source gates and demotion test.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_remaining_shadow: Any gate is missing, the sample is too small, the source class is unresolved, or performance fails its pre-registered falsifier.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — no strategy is promoted and no leaderboard score is fabricated.

title: Retain a hard joint-evidence gate for parlays and same-game combos

options.label: Multiply marginal probabilities
options.upside: Simple calculation and easy to implement.
options.downside: Assumes independence or otherwise ignores dependence; it is not validated joint evidence.

options.label: Build and validate a joint model; preserve operator rules separately
options.upside: Can measure dependence and settlement outcomes on holdouts with the correct operator context.
options.downside: Requires a sufficiently large joint sample and operator/jurisdiction-specific rule capture.

options.label: Continue to withhold combos
options.upside: Avoids presenting unsupported joint probabilities or settlement claims.
options.downside: Leaves combo strategies unavailable pending evidence.

recommendation: Continue to withhold combos until both the joint-probability model and the applicable operator settlement rules are validated. Do not infer joint quality from a parlay guide's void-leg rule.
what_supports_recommendation: FanDuel's void rule is operator-specific settlement guidance, not a dependence model; the inherited leaderboard already records combo entries as withheld.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_admission: The joint model is pre-registered, calibrated on chronological holdouts under a proper score, and matched to the actual operator's rules.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_withholding: No joint evidence, insufficient sample, or ambiguous operator/jurisdiction settlement keeps the combo blocked.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — combo policy and leaderboard remain unchanged.

title: Label local hashes as transcription integrity, not source-server authentication

options.label: Continue summary-only reads with a visible limitation
options.upside: Works where raw retention is not available or permitted.
options.downside: Limits independent reproduction to the recorded summary and source link.

options.label: Capture permission-compatible raw responses and metadata
options.upside: Improves reproducibility with exact final URL, response status, headers, capture time and bytes hash.
options.downside: Retention/redistribution rights and storage overhead need review.

recommendation: Keep the current explicit summary-only caveat; for future reads, use a rights-reviewed capture template and never claim a local note hash proves source-server bytes.
what_supports_recommendation: The current source note records approximate minute windows but no full HTTP responses, headers or exact request times.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_raw_archives: Terms permit raw retention and a capture process stores exact request/response metadata plus a deterministic hash.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_summary_only: Terms prohibit retaining source bytes or no reliable capture channel is available; retain the visible limitation and do not overstate verification.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — this review preserves its summary-only limitation and does not archive restricted source material.

title: Normalize historical club aliases before any per-team result join

options.label: Exact code join only
options.upside: Avoids silently changing a source code when the mapping is unclear.
options.downside: Leaves known legacy aliases unmatched and can drop club appearances from team-level calculations.

options.label: Versioned, source-backed alias map
options.upside: Preserves the raw source code while mapping documented historical names to the official standings identity; tests can require 32/32 reconciliation.
options.downside: Requires an explicit map, source for each mapping and a policy for ambiguous or retired codes.

options.label: Manual one-off replacement
options.upside: Quick to patch a known case.
options.downside: Hard to audit, easy to forget in a new desk, and can conceal future aliases.

recommendation: Keep raw codes immutable; apply a versioned, cited alias map in a separate normalization field; fail closed on unknown codes and require club-by-club reconciliation before team-level features are published.
what_supports_recommendation: The older e46 feed has 9 `LAR` and 9 `ARI` appearances while the official standings codes are `LA` and `AZ`; an exact join misses 18 club appearances. The newer prior desk's corrected feed demonstrates a separate code set but was not rebuilt here after the latest result delta.

what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_normalization: Each legacy-to-current mapping is documented, row counts reconcile, and every team-level result matches same-cut official standings after normalization.
what_would_change_our_mind_if.toward_no_mapping: A code is ambiguous, unsupported by an official identity source, or causes any club-level count/record mismatch; preserve it as unmatched and block downstream per-team use.

implementation_state: PROPOSAL ONLY — no results feed, alias map or other session's data was modified.
